evidence.intree_statement: Lemma sections_are_monic : Section f -> Monic f.  (* Section f = f has a left inverse `section` with section ∘ f ≈ id; conclusion f is monic *)
Lemma retractions_are_epic : Retraction f -> Epic f.  (* Retraction f = f has a right inverse `retract` with f ∘ retract ≈ id; conclusion f is epic *)

Definition flip_Section `(f : x ~> y) (s : @Section C x y f) : @Retraction C y x section.  (* the left inverse `section` of f is itself a split epi (its right inverse is f), so by retractions_are_epic the left inverse of f is epic -- exactly the remark's second clause *)

statement_record.book: If f:A->B has a left inverse g:B->A (gf=1_A) then f is monic and g is epic (an easy exercise generalizing 'every iso is mono and epi').
statement_record.intree: Theory/Morphisms.v: `sections_are_monic : Section f -> Monic f` (an f with a left inverse is monic) and `retractions_are_epic : Retraction f -> Epic f`; `flip_Section` exhibits the left inverse of f as a Retraction, so it too is Epic. Both halves of the remark are proven.
statement_record.strength_comparison: same. `Section f` packages precisely 'f has a left inverse g with g∘f ≈ id' and yields Monic f; and via flip_Section that left inverse g is a Retraction, hence Epic. Setoid-faithful (≈ in place of =).

verifier.notes: CONFIRMED. Evidence verified: Morphisms.v:179 sections_are_monic, :162 retractions_are_epic, :230 flip_Section (exhibits the left inverse of f as a Retraction => Epic). Both halves (f monic, g epic) proven, setoid-faithful. Blind pass found identical evidence.

evidence.intree_statement: Class Section `(f : x ~> y) := { section : y ~> x; section_comp : section ∘ f ≈ id }.  (* f is a split monomorphism; `section` is its retraction / left inverse *)
Class Retraction `(f : x ~> y) := { retract : y ~> x; retract_comp : f ∘ retract ≈ id }.  (* f is a split epimorphism; `retract` is its section / right inverse *)
Definition SplitEpi `(f : x ~> y) := Retraction f.  Definition SplitMono `(f : x ~> y) := Section f.

Class SplitIdempotent {x y : C} := { split_idem_retract := y; split_idem_r : x ~> split_idem_retract; split_idem_s : split_idem_retract ~> x; ... }  (* the mediating retract OBJECT y, exposed as split_idem_retract *)

statement_record.book: A split mono (resp. split epi) is an arrow with a left (resp. right) inverse; if es=1_A then s is a section (splitting) of e and e is a retraction of s, and A is a retract of X.
statement_record.intree: Theory/Morphisms.v: `Section f` (= SplitMono, f with a left inverse), `Retraction f` (= SplitEpi, f with a right inverse), with fields `section`/`retract` naming the inverses; flip_Section/flip_Retraction record the section/retraction duality. SplitIdempotent exposes the mediating `split_idem_retract` object.
statement_record.strength_comparison: same for split mono, split epi, section, retraction (all four notions and both aliases present, setoid-faithful). Minor presentation note: the object-level relation 'A is a retract of X' is not given a standalone named Definition (Retract A X), though its data is present via SplitIdempotent.split_idem_retract; and the library's field naming is the mirror convention (the field `section` inside `Section f` is the left inverse/retraction), which it documents explicitly in the header.
